spans.text: In the depths of the Lake of Cognition, Avernus.
A brilliant light shines upon the water, rippling with a beauty that is both timeless and eternal.
If it weren't for the flickering dark shadow, Ange would've thought she was dreaming.
Dreaming about being on a boat sailing in Heaven—the last place she should be going to.
What is this... spectacle?
Have you heard of "Nirvana"?
Ange shakes her head.
Not my field of expertise.
It is one of the Relics Agency's research areas.
Back then, Martha, a senior from my school stayed and worked at the applied physics lab after she graduated. Her work was so exceptional, she got recruited by the Relics Agency.
This happened to be her main project.
Creating a replica of "Nirvana" —the human connectome project then known as the "Holy Grail".
Creating the Nytos' consciousness—the Virtual Cognition Image and Lake of Cognition—to simulate logic, emotions, and instincts.
This... is the deepest part of all Nytos' consciousness—the Lake of Cognition.
What's that iceberg up there?
...Martha encountered a lot of setbacks in her research. There was a time when one could move freely among the three layers...
Until Sana's brain death.
I wanted to save her.
If you had known Martha back in those days, you would know just how brilliant, just how dazzling she was.
When such a person begged you for help, there's no way you could refuse.
I designed a device—the Evangel Axis.
A device to anchor her consciousness.
I extracted Sana's memories.
Then using the Evangel Axis, I separated her memories from the Virtual Cognition Image.
I deposited the memories here as a simulation of a human's consciousness.
In the beginning, the conduit effect of the Evangel Axis manifested as just a thin layer of ice.
But then... as more and more consciousnesses got placed here, the ice also grew thicker.
And now... it has become an entire iceberg.
...Why are you here?
...Call it the experimenter's weird quirk.
Just as how some construction workers would carve their name on roof tiles...
Gray left a duplicate of her own memories here.
That's me. I possess all her memories up until 2051.
If a human's consciousness is anchored here and given control over different physical bodies... isn't that a form of immortality?
I once believed so.
But sadly, this is no immortality.
...It certainly looks like it.
Let's say a person has her memories duplicated at the age of 10, 20, and 30, creating Copies A, B, and C. Which copy do you think is the real her?
The last copy.
No... No one knows which is the so-called "last" copy.
If the 20-year-old and 40-year-old versions of "her" take control of two different physical bodies and start making different choices individually, which of them do you think is her?
...Humans are unique and capable of genuine creativity.
The puppets powered by the Evangel Axis aren't.
To put it in simple terms... The so-called personalities formed here are only a hodgepodge of selected and shuffled traits.
They are not genuine creations.
The Evangel Axis can generate an infinite number of English words using the existing alphabet, but it cannot create a 27th letter.
Humans... cannot create an imitation of the true Creator.
What happened then?
The surgical procedure failed.
I did anchor Sana's consciousness here so that she could attempt to control a physical body via the Evangel Axis.
But it didn't work.
The generated personality was incomplete. I kept synthesizing and recombining, shuffling and rearranging...
But in the end, I realized that I had failed hopelessly.
The thing that I created... was not Sana at all.
I explained this to Martha as I despaired.
And that... was the last thing I remember.
That's why you said you're a "moment".
That moment.
Yes...
It only takes a moment to be transported here, while a human is defined by infinite moments.
So how could such a thing be human at all?
Paradeus has been harvesting humans for experimentation... in order to achieve immortality?
...It could also be a side effect.
What do you mean?
This is purely conjecture, but I think it's a side effect of this design.
Human science and experiments are essentially about imitating nature and searching for some kind of logical "truth" behind it.
For example, plants need sunlight to grow.
Nature is the sun that provides sunlight.
Scientists create grow lights through imitation and innovation.
We make plants grow with these grow lights.
However... grow lights consume electricity.
This energy consumption is a side effect of creating an imitation.
In other words, the side effect of simulating "Nirvana" via the "Holy Grail" is that it must consume bioenergy.
...How could you design something so abominable?!
...As I said, Sertürner's first experimented on isolating morphine to create an analgesic. No one could foresee the opening of Pandora's box.
I tried to decipher the code of immortality, but ended up creating this... abomination.
Back then, I sourced the required bioenergy from animals. Sana could nod and shake her head, nothing else...
But now...
Judging by the thickness of the ice, I gather the experiment was eventually a success. But it consumed a tremendous amount of energy.
Tremendous enough to create this spectacle.
It worked indeed. It created the so-called Nytos.
Why are you telling me this?
To explain why this isn't immortality.
I don't know the thought process of the "me" who remains human.
I think the miracle named "Nyto" is a deadly temptation for all scientists.
In fact, I must admit that hearing about its success still fills me with a vague sense of triumph.
However...
My reason and morals tell me that this technology should never have been taken this far.
It is unethical and utterly against my initial design.
So you're confessing out of guilt?
...I have witnessed too many real deaths here.
The Evangel Axis is not a closed-loop system. It requires external energy input.
So after a while, you will be deconstructed and consumed by the Evangel Axis as it continues to run...
You may be chosen as material for synthesizing a new "consciousness".
Or you may be transformed into energy to be fed to the Evangel Axis...
I don't know who you are.
But you're the first person to recognize me.
What is your full name?
Gray Blackwell.
I knew it...
You're Martha Meitner's junior alumnus, the author of the letters in my head.
Letters?
Dear Blackwell, It has been a long time since our last correspondence.
For whatever reason, even in this technologically advanced age, I still prefer maintaining our relationship using more traditional means.

You probably don't want to hear any more about this, but I've got to share with you how I feel right now. Perhaps I was too weak and cowardly. It was already technologically feasible back then, but I was simply too scared. I considered waiting until all the preparations were complete, but... the situation doesn't allow it.
It is time I gave up some things. Giving up does not lead to losses. On the contrary, we gain more by giving up. This is my latest epiphany.
When all human morality, our very sense of good and evil, is utterly lost, I do not see any hope in saving humanity.
Dear Martha...
This is a betrayal of our ideals. We are no longer fellow travelers sharing the same adventure. I'm sorry.
Eastern Tower Operating Level, Avernus.
With RO635's help, Koleda successfully hacks the database and obtains the security clearance to open the lock.
Error.
Unfortunately, the door to the white glass room remains firmly shut.
I knew it... The lock can only be fully disengaged by also inputting the passcode from the inside... This is the worst-case scenario.
Then we...
We have no choice but to wait for her to regain consciousness. There's nothing to be done.
Was the figure who fought alongside us in Level II really Ange?
It was her.
But I'm not entirely sure how a human could manage it.
It's because of "Hela"...
RO635 dares not... and has no desire to imagine what Ange has gone through.
Click.
The communicator suddenly makes a sound, breaking the dull silence.
Operation Aeneas Conference Room reactivated.
Task Force Aeneas registration completed – Unicorn.
Task Force Aeneas registration completed – Umbrella.
Aeneas Conference Room current progress...
Phase 1 – 100% completed.
Phase 2 – 50% completed.
Phase 3 – 0% completed.
Phase 4 – 100% completed.
Phase 5 – 0% completed.
Phase 0 – 99%... 100% completed.
RO635 is so shocked, she only manages to answer in acknowledgment after a good few seconds.
RO, it's me.
RO635 feels like crying. She has a ton of questions to ask UMP45, but once she opens her mouth, everything she wants to say is lodged in her throat.
...What's the situation on your end?
I'm okay for the moment. I can keep the Aeneas Conference Room up and running.
Can you get in touch with the others?
No one else is online.
...I see.
I'll keep trying to get through to them.
What about you? Have you found Ange?
I have, but we can't get her out yet.
I... We're working on it.
Figures... When have our missions ever been easy?
But we're counting on you.
...I won't let you down.
I'll support you remotely.
Right, I'll send you info about the lab in a bit.
No problem.
What?
RO, I have a request.
What request?
Nevermind. Even if I don't say anything, you'll do your best to sort this out.
I will.
Good luck, RO.
The Aeneas Conference Room falls silent again, but RO635 now finds calm in this silence.
Lake of Cognition, Avernus.
After listening to the letters, Gray Blackwell lapses into a long silence.
If it weren't for the constantly flowing water all around her, Ange would've thought that the world had frozen.
It appears that...
Martha did not terminate the project.
She simply renamed it from "Holy Grail" to "Hela".
Yeah.
I have a question.
Yes?
...Am I still leading the project?
Not exactly. You're a Nyto out in the physical world...
Ange thinks for a second with her eyes closed.
No...
You died long ago. Your students organized a grand funeral for you.
...That's nice.
I'm glad I resisted the temptation.
I stayed true to myself.
I did not break the Hippocratic Oath.
She mutters softly to herself. Ange cannot see her face... but she can sense her emotions faintly.
...What's my epitaph?
We're not exactly friends, so I didn't pay much attention.
But I know it's something pretty long.
...I suppose my students decided on it.
It's probably my favorite motto.
The Hippocratic Oath?
No, I'm guessing it's this...
"Death is the one thing we cannot escape; life is the one thing we cannot defile."
Thank you for telling me everything.
In return, I have a gift for you.
Hm?
Didn't you say you must go back?
I can briefly negate the effect of the Evangel Axis for you.
Then why didn't you do that earlier?
It can only be done once...
Imagine how ice floes floating on the surface of the ocean blown apart by the wind would soon drift back together.
I can only give you a moment as brief as the wind.
Also, if you can't find your way back into your body, you may get sucked back here again...
If that happens, you'll be stuck here for good.
Are you ready?
...Ready.
Take my hand... Don't let go.
